reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its purpose is to investigate and warn about a purported crypto-game promotion through malware analysis and awareness. The payment-for-review proposal, downloaded archive, antivirus warning, request to disable antivirus protection, and questionable project information are presented as evidence in the investigation rather than as an endorsement of the offer.

citations.quote: Don't try to go to any of these websites yourself or download any of this stuff.
Every interaction that I had with this site was in a carefully controlled sandbox environment
They proceeded to DM me, offering me payment in exchange for a 20 minute review of their game.
The download link for the game is locked behind a password

opening.argument: The central offer is a direct reward-for-action proposition: a purported project manager offers payment for a 15–20 minute game video, discussion of the project, and links in the description. The requested activity then escalates to launching the supplied game file and sending proof of launch. That is a concrete payment pathway tied to reviewing and executing downloaded software, not merely discussion of cryptocurrency. The archive is visibly presented as a game, while the accompanying analysis reports that running its executable immediately infected the computer and that the file could steal credentials. The promised payment therefore functions as bait for a risky action whose apparent destination is materially different from the advertised game.

citations.quote: They proceeded to DM me, offering me payment in exchange for a 20 minute review of their game.
they said that they would send me money as soon as I could send a screenshot of me launching the game.
Upon running the .exe file, a command prompt window will open for less than a second and then immediately close. This is all that it takes for our computer to become completely infected.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning language does not erase the underlying solicitation. The evidence shows an offer of payment for a review and a further condition requiring proof that the executable was launched. Calling the interaction a sandbox investigation describes the narrator's precautions, but it does not change what the sender asked a recipient to do or the reward attached to that action. The password-protected download is part of that workflow, not evidence that no solicitation occurred.

citations.quote: They proceeded to DM me, offering me payment in exchange for a 20 minute review of their game.
they said that they would send me money as soon as I could send a screenshot of me launching the game.
The download link for the game is locked behind a password

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The payment request was presented as evidence of the suspected scam, not as an offer to viewers. The narrator expressly warned people not to visit the sites or download the files and said the interaction occurred in a controlled sandbox. Those facts show the video is documenting a dangerous solicitation and discouraging the requested action; they do not establish that the video itself asks viewers to launch the file or claims they will receive payment.

citations.quote: Don't try to go to any of these websites yourself or download any of this stuff.
Every interaction that I had with this site was in a carefully controlled sandbox environment
Most importantly, never download and run any suspicious files

opening.argument: The offer combines unusually attractive compensation with multiple concrete danger signals. The displayed chat shows a purported manager offering "+250 ETH payment" while requiring a promotional game video and project links. The supplied archive is labeled as a beta game, but an antivirus window visibly reports "Threat removed" in the same file-analysis sequence. The report screen also identifies access to cryptocurrency files or wallets and possible credential harvesting. In combination, the promised reward is not a benign giveaway: it is attached to a download-and-launch path involving a file flagged by security software and behavior associated with valuable account or wallet data. The warning signs reinforce that the reward is designed to make the risky action seem worthwhile.

citations.quote: They then asked me to disable my antivirus, and assured me it was completely safe.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account treats each red flag as if it were only educational context, but their combination is the point. A purported manager offers substantial crypto compensation, asks for a promotional video and project links, and then asks that antivirus protection be disabled after detection. The fact that the narrator labels the material a warning does not make those signals less characteristic of a deceptive reward-linked download.

citations.quote: after having my antivirus detect these files, I reached back out to Nancy.
They then asked me to disable my antivirus, and assured me it was completely safe.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual warnings and malware findings are not promises made to viewers; they are investigative evidence explaining why viewers should avoid the offer. The sender's request to disable antivirus is quoted as a suspicious response, while the narrator explicitly cautions against downloading or running suspicious files. Risk signals can establish that the underlying offer is dangerous without turning a warning video into a solicitation.

citations.quote: Don't try to go to any of these websites yourself or download any of this stuff.
Also – don't trust someone just because they came from a company with a lot of TWITTER followers and Discord Server members
never download suspicious files and definitely don't run them

opening.argument: Although the narrator calls this an investigation, the material still reproduces the mechanics of a paid promotional campaign: a project representative offers compensation, specifies a video length and talking points, and requests links to the project. The video also displays the named game archive and launcher, giving the audience a concrete product and participation route to understand. That framing can function as promotion even when the narrator later criticizes it, because it packages the offer, the product, and the reward in one readily recognizable pathway. The dangerous outcome does not negate the promotional structure; it shows why that structure is deceptive.

citations.quote: They proceeded to DM me, offering me payment in exchange for a 20 minute review of their game.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the speaker an investigator overlooks how much promotional framing remains: the audience sees the project identity, the game files, the payment offer, the required review format, and the requested project links. A disclaimer about personal precautions does not remove the promotional pathway being presented. The content can warn and still materially function as an advertisement for a paid crypto-game opportunity by foregrounding its offer and participation steps.

citations.quote: They proceeded to DM me, offering me payment in exchange for a 20 minute review of their game.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The alleged promotional structure is shown so it can be scrutinized, not adopted. The narrator says the contact was a scam, warns against visiting the sites or downloading anything, and explains that the supposed game was analyzed as spyware. Those are incompatible with steering viewers toward participation. Showing a product's name or a scammer's requested talking points does not amount to endorsing the product or promising viewers the payment.
